entities.name: PMID:25446808
observations: Two prospective renal-transplant cohorts tested sCD30 before and after transplantation; sCD30 did not distinguish patients with late acute rejection after tacrolimus discontinuation from non-rejectors, and 3-month sCD30 did not predict late rejection.
The study found no association between sCD30 and rejection after immunosuppression reduction or discontinuation; it did not support sCD30-guided safe tacrolimus tapering or withdrawal.

entities.name: PMID:28694560
observations: In a small longitudinal cohort of 45 kidney recipients, failure of sCD30 to decline by post-transplant day 4 was associated with early and late acute rejection during 5-year follow-up.
The study did not report validated discrimination metrics or establish clinical utility for guiding immunosuppression reduction.

entities.name: PMID:25478957
observations: A 59-patient study found that a six-molecule soluble co-signaling signature including sCD30 was associated with long-term graft outcome; this was not evidence for sCD30 alone predicting late rejection or guiding tapering.

entities.name: PMID:32256486
observations: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 observational studies involving 1,453 patients found associations between post-transplant sCD30 and mainly early acute rejection, with heterogeneous evidence and no proof of safe immunosuppression reduction.

entities.name: sCD30 late rejection
observations: Direct prospective evidence found that 3-month sCD30 did not predict late acute rejection after renal transplantation.
A small unvalidated cohort associated failure of day-4 decline with late rejection, so findings are inconsistent and insufficient for clinical prediction.

entities.name: sCD30 tapering safety
observations: No retrieved human study demonstrated successful sCD30-guided immunosuppression minimization.
The directly relevant prospective study found sCD30 could not identify patients who could safely discontinue tacrolimus at 6 months.
